chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Baseer who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who dies while he is healthy and affluent, and has not performed Hajj, then he is from those of whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: And We will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment blind.'
I said, 'Glory be to Allah, blind?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would blind him from the path of Truth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of delaying Hajj when one is able to perform it?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) to emphasize that neglecting Hajj while possessing the means constitutes a major spiritual deficiency. The Imam clarifies that the 'blindness' mentioned in the Quran is metaphorical, signifying a loss of spiritual insight and deviation from the path of Truth, rather than physical impairment. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that Hajj is not merely a ritual but a crucial test of obedience and spiritual awareness.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Zyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The one who dies and he is of good health, affluent, not having had performed Hajj, so he is from the one whom Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Speaks of [20:124] and We will Resurrect him on the Day of Judgement, blind’.
I said, ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Blind?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Blind him away from the path of Truth’.
en.sarwar: 6. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘If one dies without performing al-Hajj when in good health and wealthy, he is one of those about whom Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has said, ‘We will, on the Day of Judgment, raise him blind.’ [20:124]

I (the narrator) then said, ‘Allah is free of all defects. Will he be raised blind?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, blind he will be raised. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has turned him blind toward the true path.’”
